answers.answer: Use lookup.weather with the city as its one argument, and lookup.currency with three arguments split by a bar: the amount, the currency to convert from and the currency to convert to. A field after a dot picks one fact, for example .temp for weather. For a currency rate alone, use lookup.currency.rate with the two currencies.

You must know how to write a reply with template braces and arguments. The page sends you to Variables and templates first. You must also know whether the bot runs in saas mode, because weather and time do not work there. You ask whoever runs the bot.
answers.quote: If braces and arguments are new to you, read Variables and templates first.

answers.answer: A working lookup prints the answer, such as Amsterdam: 12 °C, light rain. When it fails, what chat shows tells you why. Braces printed as written mean the lookup itself is wrong. A note in brackets means the service gave no answer. Nothing at all means the answer is real but empty.
answers.quote: What chat shows when a lookup has no answer tells you the cause.

answers.answer: For the weather command, the reply is {lookup.weather:{args}}, so !weather New York gives the weather in New York. For the currency command, the reply is {lookup.currency:{args.1}|{args.2}|{args.3}}, so !convert 25 USD EUR gives the converted amount. The amount must use a dot for decimals and be between 0 and one trillion. The currency codes have three letters. If an argument is wrong, the braces print as written.
answers.quote: For a currency command, put {lookup.currency:{args.1}|{args.2}|{args.3}} in the reply.

answers.answer: I did not have to guess at any step. The amount rules come right after the currency example and before the command recipe, so I learned them in time. The page does not say what happens when a viewer types a comma decimal, such as 25,50. I would reread the failure section to find that the braces print, which costs one short detour.
answers.quote: Write the amount with a dot for decimals, from 0 up to one trillion.

answers.answer: The long list of what each Twitch field gives for a login that does not exist is hard to follow when read aloud. A weather or currency user does not need it. It costs some attention, but it does not block the task.
answers.quote: For a Twitch login that does not exist, game, title, display, avatar, createdAt and followage give it.
